newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MONEY, BOND MARKETS IDLE, ECU/DRS OFF HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MONEY, BOND MARKETS IDLE, ECU/DRS OFF HIGHS.

text.p: Greek money rates and forex forwards were fluctuating narrowly in late trade and ecu/drachma had come off intraday highs to trade around 304.10/20, dealers said. Bonds were little changed.
"It was a very quiet day with money rates and forex forwards holding morning levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Bond dealers said trading activity was subdued with recently auctioned seven-year FRNs due 2004 priced between 100.50 and 101.
"The market has yet to decide whether gross or net accrual interest from bonds, FRNs will be calculated and there was an accord to settle all deals on January 28," said a bond dealer.

The auction of 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 12.40 percent produced an average accepted bid of 101.04. Another 75 billion drachmas were allocated in non-competitive bids.

The auction of the three-year, 10.20 percent coupon bond produced an average accepted bid of 99.91. The finance ministry allocated 120 billion drachmas in competiitve bid and 36 billion drachmas in non-competitive bids.
The mark was quoted at 156.64/74 drachmas from Monday's 156.560 fix, the dollar at 256.56/67 drachmas from 256.320 and the Ecu at 303.95/05 from 303.900 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma is trading around 304.10/20 in late dealings off earlier 304.30/40," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "A London-based player came out buying ecus for drachmas around mid-session which pushed ecu/drachma higher to 304.30/40."
